VIM makes detection explicitly dependent on false-positive and false-negative probabilities. [7] ICH Q2(R2) describes, among several approaches, linear-response estimates DL = 3.3σ/S and QL = 10σ/S . Here σ is an appropriate response standard deviation and S is the slope. [6] In a separate constructed example, σ = 0.003 and S = 0.050 mL/ng give DL = 0.198 ng/mL and QL = 0.600 ng/mL . These are model-based estimates, not new validated limits for the earlier 1–10 ng/mL example. Low-level samples and a declared validation plan must establish the usable limit. Report what the number supports Repeated agreement describes precision under specified conditions; it does not eliminate bias. [8] For an invented reference concentration of 10.0 ng/mL, measurements 9.0, 9.1, and 8.9 ng/mL average 9.0 ng/mL. They cluster closely but their mean is 1.0 ng/mL below the reference, or −10%. This demonstrates why repeat injections alone cannot establish quantitative accuracy. Report the analyte definition, units, sample denominator, response, standards, calibration range, dilution, quality-control outcome, and uncertainty or validated performance statement. Retain below-range and above-range flags instead of converting them automatically to zero. Identity confidence, false discovery rate , and concentration uncertainty answer different questions. Check your understanding Two analytes have identical areas. Are their concentrations equal? Not from those areas alone. Each analyte can have a different response relationship. You need suitable analyte-specific calibration, or evidence that a proposed shared model is valid. Does dividing by an internal standard produce an absolute concentration? No. It produces a response ratio. A calibrated relationship and the relevant sample-volume or mass factors are still needed to express concentration.

title: 定量测量与校准
summary: 通过明确的校准模型、适当标准、已验证的限值及清楚的报告单位，将响应转换为浓度。
text: 通过模型把信号转换为量值 质谱仪报告离子信号。要报告浓度，必须把明确定义的响应与明确定义的被测量联系起来，被测量就是打算测量的量。例如，“血浆中化合物 X 的浓度，单位 ng/mL”与“每毫克总蛋白对应的 X 信号”不同。比较样品前，应先确定分母。响应的倍数变化并不自动等于浓度的倍数变化，尤其不能直接用于不同化合物之间的比较。 校准先建立标准与示值之间的关系，再利用这一关系获得测量结果。它与调节仪器不是同一操作。 校准曲线 描述响应与量值之间的关系，但曲线本身不包含全部测量不确定度信息。 [1] [2] 本指南讨论浓度校准，不同于为准确赋予 m/z 值而进行的 质量轴校准 。 选择响应与参照 首先确定哪些数据进入计算：积分得到的前体离子信号、一个或多个产物离子信号，或相对于 内标 的比值。标准与未知样品应使用相同定义。保持积分边界及干扰检查的一致性；错误谱峰得到的精密数值仍然是错误测量。 内标加入每个待测样品，提供参照响应。分析物的稳定同位素标记形式往往有用，但仍需检验适用性、同位素纯度及可能的干扰。ICH M10 在受监管药物生物分析的范围内讨论这些检查；其适用范围与接受规则不应整体照搬到探索性组学中。 [3] 比值可以补偿分析物与内标共同经历的变化，不能纠正只改变其中一者的影响。 计算示例：反解校准关系 构造的教学示例： 假定待测溶液在 1–10 ng/mL 范围内的线性响应已得到验证。令 y = 分析物峰面积 / 内标峰面积 ， c 为以 ng/mL 表示的浓度。规定的关系为 y = 0.020 + 0.050c 。截距无量纲，斜率单位为 mL/ng。下表仅说明该方程，不足以验证真实方法。 内标加入量固定时构造的校准数值 c / ng/mL 响应比 y 1 0.070 2 0.120 5 0.270 10 0.520 未知样品得到 y = 0.320 ，因此 c = (0.320 − 0.020) / 0.050 = 6.0 ng/mL 。若原样品通过另行验证的稀释程序稀释了五倍，则原样品浓度为 5 × 6.0 = 30 ng/mL 。曲线适用于稀释后的溶液，最终报告则指向原样品。两种浓度及稀释倍数都应记录。 忽略截距会得到 0.320 / 0.050 = 6.4 ng/mL ，相对于规定的 6.0 ng/mL 高估约 6.7%。因此，即使关系完全线性，非零截距也会产生影响。相反，超过 0.520 的响应位于本例支持的范围之外。不能悄悄延长直线，并把所得答案称为已验证结果。 检验模型，而不只是相关性 很高的决定系数 R 2 并不能证明模型适当。应检查残差随浓度和采集顺序的变化；残差是测量响应减去模型预测值。弯曲模式提示直线遗漏了结构，残差离散程度增加则提示方差并非常数。宽浓度范围可以产生看似很好的相关性，同时低浓度估计仍然很差。 [4] 有证据支持权重时，加权回归可处理变化的方差。凭习惯选择 1/c 或 1/c² 并不能验证相应的误差模型。重复数很少时，估计得到的权重本身也可能不可靠。 [5] 应评估标准的反算浓度及独立配制的质量控制样品，而不是选择让未知样品最“像预期”的拟合。审计记录应保留模型、权重、排除项及接受的范围。 区分检出与定量 检出限 关注在明确判定程序下的可靠检出。 定量限 关注方法低端的定量性能。看得到一个峰，并不能证明其浓度足够可靠。VIM 明确将检出与假阳性及假阴性概率联系起来。 [7] ICH Q2(R2) 描述了多种方法，其中线性响应估计式为 DL = 3.3σ/S 和 QL = 10σ/S 。σ 是适当的响应标准差，S 是斜率。 [6] 在另一个构造示例中， σ = 0.003 、 S = 0.050 mL/ng ，得到 DL = 0.198 ng/mL 、 QL = 0.600 ng/mL 。这些只是基于模型的估计，不能据此为前述 1–10 ng/mL 示例建立新的已验证限值。可用限值必须通过低浓度样品及预先声明的验证方案来确立。 报告数值真正支持的结论 重复测量的一致性描述规定条件下的精密度，并不能消除偏倚。 [8] 假设参考浓度为 10.0 ng/mL，构造的测量值为 9.0、9.1 和 8.9 ng/mL，均值为 9.0 ng/mL。结果彼此接近，但均值比参考值低 1.0 ng/mL，即 −10%。这说明仅靠重复进样不能确立定量准确度。 报告分析物定义、单位、样品分母、响应、标准、校准范围、稀释、质控结果，以及不确定度或已验证的性能说明。保留低于或高于范围的标记，不要自动将其转换成零。身份置信度、 错误发现率 和浓度不确定度回答的是不同问题。 检查你的理解 两种分析物的峰面积相同，其浓度是否相等？ 不能仅凭峰面积得出结论。每种分析物可能具有不同的响应关系，需要适合该分析物的校准，或者证明所提出的共用模型有效的证据。 除以内标信号是否就得到了绝对浓度？ 没有，得到的只是响应比。还需要经过校准的关系，以及相关样品体积或质量换算因子，才能表达浓度。

title: Experimental design & replication
summary: Define independent units, preserve pairing, balance batches, and plan replication around the comparison you want to make.
text: Design the comparison before collecting spectra A larger data matrix does not necessarily contain more independent evidence. Experimental design connects the scientific question, the units being compared, and the observations the mass spectrometer records. Start with a sentence such as: “Estimate the average treatment-associated change in compound X across independently sampled donors.” That sentence identifies a target population, a contrast, and a biological level. Replacing “donors” with “injections” changes the question. Write down the endpoint, sample denominator, planned contrasts, and relevant covariates before examining group differences. Separate an observational association from an intervention effect: randomizing injection order does not randomize a person's exposure or disease status. Reporting standards for metabolomics explicitly include sample collection, matching, acquisition scheduling, and the model-validation scheme. [1] Identify the units in the hierarchy A biological unit is the entity about which a conclusion is intended. An experimental unit is independently assigned to an intervention. An observational unit is what is measured. These can coincide, but they need not. Several measurements from one experimental unit do not become independent treatment assignments. Lazic and colleagues show why this distinction is more informative than simply labelling everything “biological” or “technical.” [2] For example, individually treated cultures can be experimental units; cultures treated together through one shared vessel may not be. Repeated sampling from a donor adds information about that donor over time, not new donors. Record the hierarchy explicitly: donor, culture, aliquot, preparation, and injection, as applicable. A biological replicate label should explain which level was independently sampled or generated and how treatment was assigned. Constructed counting example: eight independently sampled donors each provide one sample. Two aliquots from each sample are prepared separately, and each preparation is injected three times. There are 8 × 2 × 3 = 48 injections , 8 × 2 = 16 preparations , and 8 donors . For a comparison across donors, the independent donor count is eight, not 48. The extra measurements help investigate lower-level variation. Balance conditions across nuisance factors A batch effect is systematic measurement variation associated with processing or acquisition groups. If every control is in one batch and every treated sample in another, their difference cannot by itself distinguish biology from batch. Prevention is therefore part of the experiment, not merely a later normalization choice. When a nuisance factor can be controlled, blocking places the conditions of interest within comparable groups; randomization distributes remaining uncontrolled influences rather than deliberately aligning them with condition. NIST describes the randomized-block principle and its analysis. [3] Randomization does not guarantee perfect balance in a small experiment. Check the generated allocation and document any restrictions without rearranging it to favor a desired result. Constructed balanced allocation of 12 independent units; counts are not a power recommendation Processing batch Control units Treated units Total A 2 2 4 B 2 2 4 C 2 2 4 Here each batch contains both conditions and the study has six units per condition. Randomize the feasible processing or acquisition order within the plan. With an additive model containing an intercept, condition, and two indicators for the three batches, the design has four independent columns. A different allocation with controls only in A and treated units only in B makes condition and batch identical columns: no arithmetic can estimate their separate effects from those observations alone. The balanced design helps identifiability; it does not guarantee sufficient precision or eliminate interactions. Preserve pairing and repeated measurements If the same donor is measured before and after an intervention, the relevant contrast may be a within-donor change. Keep the donor identifier in the analysis rather than treating all measurements as unrelated. More complex hierarchies may require mixed-effects or other design-appropriate models. NIST's treatment of nested variation illustrates why observations at different levels have different sources of variation. [4] Constructed paired example: three donors have before values [10, 100, 1000] and after values [20, 200, 2000] in the same arbitrary units. Every donor doubles, so every within-donor log 2 ratio equals 1. Their absolute changes are [10, 100, 1000] , with mean 1110 / 3 = 370 . Mean log ratio and mean absolute change are different estimands. Neither is universally preferable; choose the one that answers the scientific question. The three donors do not become six independent biological units. Choose replication for the intended inference There is no universally sufficient number of replicates. Planning depends on the effect worth detecting or the precision needed, expected between-unit variation, the design, and the tolerated decision errors. NIST's sample-size examples make these dependencies explicit. [5] A pilot can inform variation estimates, but a small pilot estimate is uncertain. Explore plausible ranges and include expected attrition or unusable measurements. Use technical repetition where it diagnoses an important part of the measurement process. If between-donor variability dominates the question, many more injections of the same donors may give little additional information about the wider population. If the measurement is unstable, additional donors alone will not repair it. Budget controls, calibration, and independent units together; distinguish discovery work from a separately designed confirmation study. Make the analysis respect the design Prespecify exclusions. Define failed-run and unusable-sample criteria without consulting the desired group effect; document deviations. Preserve identifiers. Link every injection to its preparation and biological origin. Do not average away pairing or silently count technical repeats as new units. Keep evaluation independent. For donor-level prediction, keep all observations from a donor together when splitting training and test sets. Learned preprocessing belongs inside the training procedure. Define the testing family. Thousands of feature-wise comparisons require an appropriate multiple-testing strategy. FDR control does not fix confounding or pseudoreplication. Retain missingness information. Record why observations are unavailable when known; see missing values before choosing a handling strategy. These are design-aware consequences of defining units and a validation scheme, not a universal statistical recipe. Publish the allocation and metadata needed to reconstruct the comparison, together with effect estimates and their uncertainty. Check your understanding Can six reinjections rescue a study with one independent unit per condition? They can reveal injection repeatability for those units. They cannot estimate biological variation across independently replicated units, so they do not rescue that population-level comparison. Does random injection order remove all batch effects? No. It reduces systematic alignment with order but does not stop drift or processing differences. Controls and suitable modelling remain necessary.

title: 实验设计与重复
summary: 定义独立单位、保留配对、平衡批次，并围绕预期比较规划重复。
text: 采集谱图之前先设计比较 更大的数据矩阵不一定包含更多独立证据。实验设计把科学问题、被比较的单位以及质谱仪记录的观测联系起来。可以先写一句话，例如：“估计在独立抽样的供者群体中，化合物 X 与处理相关的平均变化。”这句话指定了目标总体、比较以及生物学层级。把“供者”换成“进样”就改变了问题。 在查看组间差异之前，写明终点、样品分母、计划比较及相关协变量。应区分观察性关联与干预效应：随机化进样顺序并不会随机化一个人的暴露或疾病状态。代谢组学报告标准明确涵盖样品采集、匹配、采集顺序安排及模型验证方案。 [1] 识别层级中的不同单位 生物学单位是希望对其作出结论的实体；实验单位是被独立分配干预的实体；观测单位是实际接受测量的对象。三者可能一致，也可能不同。同一实验单位的多次测量并不会变成多次独立的处理分配。Lazic 等说明，这种区分比简单地把一切标记为“生物学”或“技术”重复更有信息量。 [2] 例如，分别独立施加处理的培养物可以是实验单位；通过一个共享容器一起处理的培养物则未必是。同一供者的重复采样增加了该供者随时间变化的信息，并没有增加供者数量。应明确记录供者、培养物、分装、制备及进样等适用层级。 生物学重复 的标签应说明哪个层级是独立抽样或生成的，以及如何分配处理。 构造的计数示例： 八名独立抽样的供者各提供一份样品。每份样品取两个分装分别制备，每份制备物进样三次。因此共有 8 × 2 × 3 = 48 次进样 、 8 × 2 = 16 份制备物 及 8 名供者 。对于供者间比较，独立供者数是八，而不是 48。额外测量有助于研究更低层级的变异。 在干扰因素间平衡条件 批次效应 是与处理或采集分组相关的系统性测量变化。若全部对照在一批、全部处理样品在另一批，仅凭两组差异就无法区分生物学效应与批次效应。因此，预防混杂属于实验本身，而不只是事后选择归一化方法。 当某个干扰因素可控时，区组设计将关注的条件放入可比的组内；随机化则分散其余不可控影响，避免人为将其与条件对齐。NIST 描述了随机区组原理及相应分析。 [3] 在小实验中，随机化并不保证完美平衡。应检查生成的分配，并记录限制条件，但不能为了支持预期结果而重新排列。 12 个独立单位的构造平衡分配；数量不是功效建议 处理批次 对照单位 处理单位 总数 A 2 2 4 B 2 2 4 C 2 2 4 每批都含两种条件，整个研究每种条件有六个单位。应在计划范围内随机化可行的处理或采集顺序。若采用包含截距、条件以及表示三个批次的两个指示变量的加性模型，设计具有四个线性独立的列。另一种分配若让对照只在 A 批、处理只在 B 批，条件与批次就成为相同的列：仅凭这些观测，任何计算都不能分别估计二者的效应。平衡设计有助于参数可识别性，但不保证精密度足够，也不能消除交互作用。 保留配对与重复测量关系 若同一供者在干预前后接受测量，相关比较可能是供者内变化。分析中应保留供者标识，而不是把全部测量当作彼此无关。更复杂的层级可能需要混合效应或其他与设计相符的模型。NIST 对嵌套变异的讨论说明了为何不同层级的观测具有不同的变异来源。 [4] 构造的配对示例： 三名供者的干预前数值为 [10, 100, 1000] ，干预后为 [20, 200, 2000] ，使用相同的任意单位。每名供者都翻倍，因此每个供者内的 log 2 比值都为 1。绝对变化为 [10, 100, 1000] ，均值为 1110 / 3 = 370 。平均对数比值与平均绝对变化是不同的目标量，没有哪一种普遍更优；应选择回答科学问题的目标量。三名供者不会因此变成六个独立生物学单位。 根据预期推断选择重复 不存在普遍足够的重复数。规划取决于值得检出的效应或所需精度、预期单位间变异、实验设计，以及能够容忍的判定错误。NIST 的样本量示例明确展示了这些依赖关系。 [5] 预实验可帮助估计变异，但小预实验的估计本身并不确定。应探索合理范围，并考虑预期退出或不可用测量。 技术重复应服务于对测量过程中重要环节的诊断。如果问题主要受供者间变异影响，同一批供者增加很多进样，可能只为更广泛总体提供很少额外信息。如果测量不稳定，仅增加供者也不能修复问题。应一并规划质控、校准与独立单位的预算，并区分发现性研究和另行设计的确认性研究。 让分析尊重设计 预先规定排除条件。 不参考期望组间效应来制定失败运行和不可用样品标准，并记录偏离计划之处。 保留标识。 把每次进样关联到制备物及生物学来源，不要用平均操作抹去配对关系，也不要默默把技术重复计为新单位。 保持评估独立。 对于供者层面的预测，划分训练集与测试集时，同一供者的全部观测应留在同一侧。需要从数据学习的预处理也属于训练过程。 定义检验集合。 成千上万个特征逐一比较时，需要适当的多重检验策略。 FDR 控制不能修复混杂或伪重复。 保留缺失信息。 若知道观测不可用的原因，应予以记录；选择处理策略前先了解 缺失值 。 这些是明确定义单位及验证方案后，与设计相符的推论，而非通用统计配方。应发布重建比较所需的分配与元数据，以及效应估计和相应不确定度。 检查你的理解 每种条件只有一个独立单位，增加六次重复进样能挽救研究吗？ 这些进样可以揭示相应单位的进样重复性，却不能估计独立重复单位之间的生物学变异，因此不能挽救该总体层面的比较。 随机进样顺序是否消除所有批次效应？ 不能。它减少与顺序的系统性对齐，但不会阻止漂移或处理差异。仍然需要质控及适当建模。

title: QC, batch effects & normalization
summary: Use controls to diagnose drift, test correction assumptions, and distinguish a cleaner matrix from a more defensible measurement.
text: Measure unwanted variation before correcting it Quality control (QC) asks whether the analytical system behaved acceptably for the intended measurement. Normalization changes a numerical scale using an explicit reference or assumption. Batch correction models systematic differences associated with processing groups or acquisition order. These activities overlap, but a cleaner-looking matrix is not proof that the measurements became more reliable. Start with a proposed explanation: unstable response over injection order, different loading, or a discontinuity after maintenance. Ask what evidence could distinguish that explanation from real sample variation. A batch effect can affect features differently; one multiplier need not describe the whole experiment. The goal is a defensible comparison, not identical distributions at any cost. Give each control a specific job A system-suitability sample tests whether a method is ready to run. Blanks reveal background or carryover under the conditions they represent. Repeated pooled or reference QC samples track analytical consistency. An internal standard follows the response of a defined added substance. These controls answer different questions and are not interchangeable. The mQACC recommendations emphasize describing control composition, use, placement, and acceptance criteria. [1] For a pooled QC, document which samples contribute and when pooling occurred. Reinjecting one prepared pool mainly examines variability after that preparation; separately processing pool aliquots also samples those processing steps. A component rare in study samples may be diluted below detection in a pool. Consequently, good pooled-QC behavior supports the signals the pool represents, not every possible analyte. Choose QC placement and frequency from the method's stability and the variation you need to observe. A few controls at the start cannot describe an unobserved change halfway through a long sequence. Keep a stable reference across batches when cross-batch comparison matters. Record interruptions, maintenance, run order, and control identity alongside the measurement table. Worked example: what a drift correction assumes Constructed teaching model: a chemically stable QC gives response 100 at injection 1 and 80 at injection 11 for one feature. Suppose independent evidence justifies a linear multiplicative drift model over this interval. At injection 6 the interpolated expected QC response is 100 + (6 − 1) × (80 − 100) / (11 − 1) = 90 . To express a study-sample response of 72 at that position on the injection-1 scale, calculate 72 × 100 / 90 = 80 . The corrected value is still a relative response, not a concentration. Two endpoints do not themselves establish a linear trajectory. A transient problem between them could be invisible, and a different feature may drift differently. Extrapolating beyond the observed interval adds another unsupported assumption. This arithmetic explains one correction; it does not recommend two QC injections or a particular spacing. Wehrens and colleagues compared correction strategies on several untargeted MS datasets and found that performance depended on the data and available controls. [2] In practice, assess whether enough reliable QC observations exist to support the chosen model complexity and whether the controls represent the affected signals. Choose the reference deliberately Different denominators define different results. Signal per original sample volume, signal per cell, signal per total protein, and signal relative to a pooled reference are not synonymous. A change in the denominator can change the biological interpretation even when the numerator is measured perfectly. State whether a correction addresses analytical response, sample input, or a deliberately relative biological scale. Distribution-based methods require assumptions about which parts of the measured distribution should remain stable. Median scaling is a simple example; forcing distributions to agree is a stronger constraint. In a phosphoproteomics experiment, Kauko and colleagues demonstrated how genuine broad directional changes can conflict with centering assumptions. [3] That is a reason to test assumptions, not to prohibit normalization or declare one alternative universally best. Worked example: a correction can erase a real effect Separate constructed example: four feature responses in sample A are [10, 20, 30, 40] ; sample B has [20, 40, 60, 80] . The medians are 25 and 50, so scaling B to A uses 25 / 50 = 0.5 and produces [10, 20, 30, 40] . All original B/A ratios were 2; all scaled ratios are 1. If the doubling arose entirely from a shared technical multiplier, that operation removes it in this idealized model. If all four features genuinely doubled per unit of the intended sample denominator, the same operation removes the biological change. The two numerical arrays alone cannot identify which explanation is correct. Information about sample input, appropriate standards, and the biology must supply that distinction. Evaluate correction without rewarding overfitting Plot feature responses against injection order and batch before and after correction. For a positive, ratio-scale response, one descriptive repeatability measure is CV (%) = 100 × sample standard deviation / mean . In invented QC responses [90, 100, 110] , the mean is 100 and the sample standard deviation, using divisor n − 1 , is 10; the CV is 10%. This describes those three values, not universal method acceptability. Precision depends on the measurement conditions. [6] Reduced variation among the very QCs used to fit a flexible curve can merely show that the curve fits them. Where feasible, use withheld controls or another independent check. Inspect retained biological contrasts, concentration-dependent behavior, control failures, and residual order effects. Principal-component plots are useful diagnostics, but making batch clusters disappear does not alone prove that biological information was preserved. If condition and batch are completely confounded, correction cannot discover their separate effects from those data alone. Return to experimental design rather than treating software output as evidence that the ambiguity vanished. Record model parameters and preprocessing order so the original matrix can be recovered. Keep unavailable observations visible Blank filtering, feature exclusion, drift correction, and imputation alter different parts of a dataset. A missing value is not automatically zero, and a signal absent from the pooled QC may still occur in a study sample. An imputed number is a model output rather than a new measurement. A primary proteomics benchmark found that imputation performance depends on workflow and evaluation task. [4] Compare relevant conclusions with an unimputed or otherwise appropriate alternative, preserve missingness flags, and report why a handling strategy fits the study. For prediction, learn data-dependent transformations using training data within the evaluation design. Document the complete sequence of steps, not just the final algorithm name. [5] Check your understanding Does a pooled QC with low CV establish accurate concentrations? No. It demonstrates consistency for the represented signals and conditions. Concentration accuracy requires suitable calibration and independent quantitative checks. Should normalization be chosen because it yields more significant features? No. Select it from a defensible measurement model and evaluate independent evidence. Optimizing the number of discoveries risks rewarding distortion.

title: 质控、批次效应与归一化
summary: 利用质控诊断漂移、检验校正假设，并区分更整齐的数据矩阵与更有依据的测量。
text: 先测量不需要的变异，再进行校正 质量控制（QC）考察分析系统的表现是否满足预期测量用途。归一化根据明确的参照或假设改变数值尺度。批次校正对与处理分组或采集顺序相关的系统性差异建模。这些工作相互关联，但数据矩阵看起来更整齐，并不能证明测量更可靠。 先提出一个解释，例如响应随进样顺序不稳定、上样量不同，或维护后出现突变，再询问什么证据能够区分该解释与真实样品变化。 批次效应 对不同特征的影响可能不同，一个乘数未必能够描述整个实验。目标是得到有依据的比较，而不是不惜代价让分布相同。 让每一种质控承担明确任务 系统适用性样品检验方法是否已准备好运行。空白在其所代表的条件下揭示背景或残留。重复测量混合或参考质控样品可跟踪分析一致性。 内标 跟踪明确加入物质的响应。这些质控回答不同问题，不能相互替代。mQACC 建议强调报告质控组成、用途、安排位置及接受标准。 [1] 对于混合质控，应记录由哪些样品构成，以及何时进行混合。反复进样同一份已制备的混合物，主要考察制备之后的变异；分别处理混合物的多个分装，还会覆盖相应处理步骤的变异。研究样品中较少见的组分可能在混合后被稀释到无法检出。因此，混合质控表现良好，支持的是其所代表的信号，而非一切可能的分析物。 应根据方法稳定性及需要观察的变异，选择质控位置与频率。仅在开头安排少量质控，无法描述长序列中途未被观测到的变化。跨批次比较重要时，应保持稳定的跨批次参照。将中断、维护、运行顺序及质控身份与测量表一同记录。 计算示例：漂移校正假设了什么 构造的教学模型： 化学性质稳定的质控中，某个特征在第 1 次进样的响应为 100，在第 11 次为 80。假设独立证据支持该区间内的线性乘性漂移模型。在第 6 次进样，插值得到的预期质控响应为 100 + (6 − 1) × (80 − 100) / (11 − 1) = 90 。若该位置研究样品的响应为 72，要将其表示在第 1 次进样的尺度上，可计算 72 × 100 / 90 = 80 。 校正后仍然是相对响应，并非浓度。仅凭两个端点不能确立线性轨迹，二者之间的瞬时问题可能完全不可见，其他特征也可能以不同方式漂移。超出已观察区间进行外推，会再增加一个没有支持的假设。这段计算解释一种校正，并不推荐只进样两次质控，也不推荐具体间隔。 Wehrens 等在多个非靶向质谱数据集中比较校正策略，发现表现取决于数据及可用质控。 [2] 实际应用时，应评估可靠质控观测是否足够支持所选模型复杂度，以及质控是否代表受影响的信号。 有意识地选择参照 不同分母定义不同结果。每单位原始样品体积、每个细胞、每单位总蛋白的信号，以及相对于混合参照的信号，并不是同一概念。即使分子测量完全准确，改变分母也可能改变生物学解释。应说明校正针对的是分析响应、样品投入量，还是有意选择的相对生物学尺度。 基于分布的方法要求假定测得分布的某些部分应保持稳定。中位数缩放是简单例子；强制分布一致则是更强的约束。在一项磷酸化蛋白质组实验中，Kauko 等展示了真实而广泛的同向变化如何违背中心化假设。 [3] 这说明需要检验假设，而不是禁止归一化，或宣布某种替代方法普遍最优。 计算示例：校正也能抹去真实效应 另一个构造示例： 样品 A 中四个特征的响应为 [10, 20, 30, 40] ，样品 B 为 [20, 40, 60, 80] 。中位数分别是 25 和 50，因此将 B 缩放到 A 使用 25 / 50 = 0.5 ，得到 [10, 20, 30, 40] 。原始 B/A 比值全部为 2，缩放后的比值全部为 1。 若翻倍完全由共同的技术乘数引起，这个操作在理想化模型中消除了技术变化。若相对于预期样品分母，四个特征确实都翻倍，同一操作就抹去了生物学变化。仅凭这两个数值数组无法识别哪种解释正确，必须借助样品投入量、适当标准及生物学信息来区分。 评估校正，避免奖励过拟合 校正前后都应绘制特征响应随进样顺序和批次变化的图。对于正值、具有有意义零点的比率尺度响应，一项描述性重复性指标为 CV (%) = 100 × 样本标准差 / 均值 。构造的质控响应 [90, 100, 110] 的均值为 100，使用 n − 1 作分母的样本标准差为 10，因此 CV 为 10%。这仅描述三个数值，不是方法可接受性的通用标准。精密度取决于测量条件。 [6] 如果使用灵活曲线拟合某些质控，这些相同质控在校正后变异减少，可能仅说明曲线拟合了它们。可行时，应使用未参与拟合的质控或其他独立检查。检查保留下来的生物学比较、浓度相关行为、质控失败及残余顺序效应。主成分图有助于诊断，但批次聚类消失本身不能证明生物学信息得以保留。 若条件与批次完全混杂，仅凭这些数据，校正无法发现二者各自的效应。应回到 实验设计 ，而不是把软件输出视为歧义已经消失的证据。记录模型参数及预处理顺序，使原始矩阵仍可恢复。 保留不可用观测的信息 空白筛选、特征排除、漂移校正及插补改变的是数据集的不同部分。 缺失值 并不自动等于零，混合质控中缺少的信号仍可能出现在研究样品中。插补的数值是模型输出，不是新测量。一项原始蛋白质组学基准研究发现，插补表现取决于工作流程及评估任务。 [4] 应将相关结论与未插补或其他合适的替代分析比较，保留缺失标记，并报告所选处理策略为何适合该研究。对于预测，应在评估设计内部使用训练数据学习数据依赖的变换。记录完整步骤顺序，而不只是最终算法名称。 [5] 检查你的理解 混合质控的 CV 很低，是否证明浓度准确？ 不能。它说明所代表信号在相应条件下具有一致性。浓度准确性仍需要适当校准和独立定量检查。 能否因为某种归一化产生更多显著特征就选择它？ 不能。应根据有依据的测量模型选择，并用独立证据评估。以发现数量为优化目标，可能反而奖励失真。

title: Bottom-up proteomics: from sample to protein evidence
summary: Follow preparation, digestion, measurement, identification, and quantification while preserving the limits of peptide evidence.
text: Measure peptides, reason about proteins Bottom-up proteomics digests proteins into peptides before measuring them. That choice makes complex mixtures accessible to LC-MS/MS, but breaks the direct connection between a measured ion and its intact parent molecule. The useful question is therefore not simply “Which proteins are in this file?” It is “Which peptide evidence supports which protein-level statements, under this preparation and analysis?” This Guide follows that evidence through the experiment. Read the acquisition Guide for precursor selection and scan scheduling; the workflow here does not require one universally preferred acquisition mode. A protein survey, an isoform comparison, and a modification-site experiment need different evidence even when they share an instrument. Define the endpoint before preparing samples Write down the biological comparison, independent sampling unit, and intended result: a protein group, a particular sequence variant, a peptide abundance, or a localized modification. Preserve relationships among subjects, preparations, fractions, and injections. Replicating an injection tests a later step than independently preparing another sample. The experimental-design principles in the data-analysis Guide apply before any spectra exist. Choose controls that answer specific questions. A preparation blank can reveal material introduced during processing; an injection blank can test carryover; a reference digest can track the LC-MS system. These controls are complementary. In a planning exercise, ask which control would detect a failed digestion and which would detect retention-time drift. An already-digested reference may detect the latter while bypassing the former entirely. Extraction and cleanup select what can be observed Extraction must release the proteins of interest while producing material compatible with digestion and MS. Strong solubilization and clean electrospray are not the same requirement. FASP demonstrated detergent-containing extraction followed by buffer exchange and digestion on a filter. SP3 demonstrated a bead-based preparation route, including low-input applications. These are examples of solving compatibility and recovery problems, not a ranking that applies to every sample. [1] [2] Common workflows denature proteins, reduce disulfides, and alkylate available cysteines, but the exact chemistry must suit the question. Record reagent identities, order, conditions, and cleanup. Material lost to a surface or discarded fraction is absent from subsequent measurements regardless of instrument sensitivity. A chemically modified residue introduced during preparation must also be represented correctly during searching. Digestion is an experimental and computational choice Trypsin is widely used because cleavage after lysine or arginine produces a useful peptide population. Search software encodes an enzyme rule, allowed missed cleavages, and terminal specificity; these are explicit models of the digest. The original specificity study illustrates why enzyme assumptions affect candidate interpretation. Do not turn the name “trypsin” into a claim that every eligible bond was cleaved completely. [3] Constructed digestion exercise: take the sequence AKPEPTIDERAAK . Under the stated teaching rule “cleave after K or R except before P,” complete cleavage produces AKPEPTIDER and AAK . The K at position 2 is followed by P and is not a permitted cleavage here. Retaining the eligible bond after R gives the full sequence with one missed cleavage. This is a rule-based example, not a measured digestion yield. A different protease can expose complementary sequence regions, but also changes the search space and peptide behavior. Inspect the observed distribution of missed cleavages and modifications against a suitable reference. A high identification count alone cannot distinguish a well-controlled digest from a search made permissive enough to explain unexpected products. Separate, acquire, and preserve provenance Peptide cleanup and chromatographic separation influence which signals reach the source together. Fractionation can spread a mixture across runs, trading additional handling and instrument time for reduced complexity per run. Keep fraction identity and sample origin attached to each file. Pooling all fractions into a single unnamed sample loses information needed to interpret repeat observations. Record the LC method, instrument configuration, acquisition settings, and raw-file identifiers. MIAPE-MS provides reporting guidance for these measurement details. It does not certify an experiment merely because its checklist is filled in. Inspect suitable system checks and representative spectra before interpreting a larger downstream table. [4] Keep the evidence hierarchy visible An accepted peptide-spectrum match supports a sequence assignment for a spectrum. Repeated spectra can support the same peptide; a peptide can map to several proteins. Consequently, PSM counts, distinct peptide counts, and protein-group counts answer different questions. mzIdentML represents these layers and their connections rather than requiring one flattened protein list. [5] Use the identification and inference Guide to examine shared peptides and error control. A protein-level claim should retain its supporting peptides and alternative mappings. A confidently measured common peptide does not by itself identify which homolog or isoform supplied it. Nor does a partial digest reconstruct the complete combination of modifications on an intact protein. Choose a quantity that matches the question Peptide signal is an intermediate measurement. Combining peptides into a protein summary requires stated rules for shared sequences, modified forms, interference, and missing values. Preferentially detectable or proteotypic peptides can be useful measurement candidates, but observability depends on the workflow. Detectability and sequence uniqueness must be checked separately. [6] Constructed recovery example: two samples each contain 100 arbitrary amount units of the target. Recoveries of 80% and 40% leave 80 and 40 units for measurement. With equal downstream response, the observed ratio is 2 even though the starting ratio was 1. A peptide standard added after those losses cannot retrospectively measure the missing material. Stable-isotope peptide standards support calibration for the steps and analytes they actually track; AQUA provides a foundational demonstration. [7] Deliver an auditable result Report database release, contaminants and decoys, digestion and modification settings, software versions, thresholds at each reporting level, and quantitative processing. MIAPE informatics guidance supports documenting identification and validation methods. Preserve intermediate peptide-to-protein mappings alongside the final table so that a reader can inspect its assumptions. [8] Check your understanding Does twice the peptide signal prove twice the protein amount? No. First examine recovery, digestion, response, interference, and the peptide-to-protein relationship. The recovery example demonstrates one possible alternative explanation. What should travel with a protein result? The evidence and rules that produced it: peptide identities, mappings, confidence levels, quantification choices, and sample provenance. Continue to the identification and inference Guide for a worked mapping example.

title: 自下而上蛋白质组学：从样本到蛋白质证据
summary: 沿制备、酶解、测量、鉴定和定量追踪证据，同时保留肽段证据的解释边界。
text: 测量肽段，推断蛋白质 自下而上蛋白质组学先把蛋白质酶解为肽段，再进行测量。这使复杂混合物能够接受 LC-MS/MS 分析，却也打断了所测离子与完整母体分子之间的直接联系。因此，有用的问题不只是“这个文件里有哪些蛋白质？”，而是“在这套制备和分析条件下，哪些肽段证据支持哪些蛋白质层面的陈述？” 本指南沿着实验流程追踪这些证据。关于前体选择和扫描安排，请阅读 采集指南 ；这里的工作流程并不要求一种普遍最优的采集模式。蛋白质普查、异构体比较和修饰位点实验即使使用同一台仪器，也需要不同的证据。 制样之前先确定要回答的问题 写明生物学比较、独立采样单位和预期结果：蛋白质分组、某个序列变体、肽段丰度，还是已定位的修饰。保留受试对象、制备样本、组分和进样之间的关系。重复进样检验的步骤，比独立制备另一份样本更靠后。 数据分析指南中的实验设计原则 在产生任何谱图之前就适用。 为具体问题选择对照。制备空白可以揭示处理过程中引入的物质；进样空白可以检验残留；参考酶解物可以跟踪 LC-MS 系统。这些对照相互补充。在规划练习中，问自己：哪个对照能发现酶解失败，哪个能发现保留时间漂移？已经完成酶解的参考物可能发现后者，却完全绕过了前者。 提取和净化决定哪些成分有机会被观察 提取既要释放目标蛋白质，也要得到与酶解和质谱兼容的材料。充分溶解和获得干净的电喷雾信号并不是同一个要求。FASP 展示了含去污剂提取后，在滤膜上换液并酶解的路线。SP3 展示了基于磁珠的制备路线，包括低输入量应用。这些是解决兼容性与回收率问题的实例，而不是适用于所有样本的排名。 [1] [2] 常见流程包含蛋白质变性、二硫键还原和可反应半胱氨酸的烷基化，但具体化学处理必须适合研究问题。记录试剂身份、加入顺序、反应条件和净化步骤。吸附在表面或随废弃组分损失的材料，无论仪器灵敏度多高，都不会进入后续测量。制备过程中引入的残基化学修饰也必须在检索时得到正确表示。 酶解既是实验选择，也是计算选择 胰蛋白酶广泛使用，因为在赖氨酸或精氨酸之后的切割能生成适合分析的肽段群体。检索软件编码酶切规则、允许的漏切数和末端特异性；这些是对酶解物的显式模型。最初的特异性研究说明，关于酶的假设会影响候选结果的解释。不要把“胰蛋白酶”这个名称当成每个可切割键都已完全切开的证据。 [3] 构造的酶切练习： 考虑序列 AKPEPTIDERAAK 。采用明确的教学规则“在 K 或 R 之后切割，但其后为 P 时除外”，完全切割得到 AKPEPTIDER 和 AAK 。第 2 位的 K 后接 P，在此规则下不是允许的切点。若保留 R 后本可切开的键，就得到带一次漏切的完整序列。这是基于规则的例子，不是实测酶解产率。 换用另一种蛋白酶可能暴露互补的序列区域，也会改变检索空间和肽段行为。结合合适的参考，检查实测漏切和修饰的分布。鉴定数量多，本身不能区分受控良好的酶解与仅仅放宽检索条件后能够解释更多意外产物的情况。 分离、采集并保留来源信息 肽段净化和色谱分离影响哪些信号同时进入离子源。分级可把混合物分散到多次运行，以更多操作和机时换取每次运行较低的复杂度。每个文件都应保留组分身份和样本来源。把所有组分归并为一个无具体标识的样本，会丢失解释重复观察所需的信息。 记录 LC 方法、仪器配置、采集设置和原始文件标识。MIAPE-MS 为这些测量细节提供报告指导，但填完检查表并不等于实验已经通过认证。在解释庞大的下游表格前，应检查合适的系统检验结果和代表性谱图。 [4] 保留可见的证据层级 通过筛选的 肽段–谱图匹配 支持针对一张谱图的序列指认。多张谱图可能支持同一肽段；一个肽段也可能映射到多个蛋白质。因此，PSM 数、不同肽段数和蛋白质分组数回答的是不同问题。mzIdentML 表示这些层级及其联系，而不是要求把一切压成一个平面的蛋白质列表。 [5] 阅读 肽段鉴定与蛋白质推断指南 ，了解共享肽段和错误控制。蛋白质层面的陈述应保留支持它的肽段及其他可能映射。可信测得的共有肽段本身不能确定它来自哪个同源蛋白或异构体。局部酶解证据也不能重建完整蛋白质上全部修饰的共存组合。 选择与问题相符的定量对象 肽段信号是中间测量量。把多个肽段合并成蛋白质汇总值，需要说明共享序列、修饰形式、干扰和缺失值的处理规则。容易被检测到的 蛋白质代表性肽段 可作为测量候选，但可观测性取决于流程。可检测性与序列唯一性必须分别检验。 [6] 构造的回收率例子： 两份样本起初各含 100 个任意量单位的目标物。80% 和 40% 的回收率分别留下 80 和 40 单位用于测量。在下游响应相同的条件下，观测比值为 2，而起始比值为 1。损失发生后才加入的肽段标准品，不能事后测出已经丢失的材料。稳定同位素肽段标准品能为其实际跟踪的分析物和步骤提供校准；AQUA 是基础性示范。 [7] 交付可以追溯的结果 报告数据库版本、污染物与诱饵序列、酶切和修饰设置、软件版本、每个报告层级的阈值以及定量处理。MIAPE 信息学指南支持记录鉴定和验证方法。将中间的肽段–蛋白质映射与最终表格一起保存，使读者能够检查其假设。 [8] 检查你的理解 肽段信号翻倍能证明蛋白质量翻倍吗？ 不能。先检查回收率、酶解、响应、干扰和肽段与蛋白质之间的关系。回收率例子展示了另一种可能解释。 蛋白质结果应该附带什么？ 产生该结果的证据和规则：肽段身份、映射、置信度层级、定量选择及样本来源。继续阅读鉴定与推断指南中的映射实例。

title: Peptide identification and protein inference
summary: Separate scores, error levels, shared-peptide mappings, protein groups, and sequence coverage using explicit teaching examples.
text: Separate four questions Peptide identification asks which candidate explains measured evidence. Protein inference asks which parent proteins are supported by the identified peptides. Confidence estimation asks how often accepted results are wrong under a stated procedure. Modification localization asks which residue carries a modification. These questions are connected, but a good answer to one does not automatically answer the others. Start from fragment-ion evidence and the bottom-up workflow . Here, a conventional spectrum-centric database search provides the teaching model. DIA and library workflows may organize evidence differently; use the acquisition Guide for how the data were collected and inspect the actual reporting units of the analysis. A search result depends on its candidate set A database search enumerates candidate peptides under a sequence database, digestion rule, mass tolerance, and modification model. It compares expected fragment evidence with a measured MS/MS spectrum. SEQUEST's cross-correlation approach is one historical example of a scoring function; its numerical scale is specific to that method. A higher score is stronger agreement by that function, not a universal probability of correctness. [1] Inspect whether the intended organism, variants, common contaminants, and relevant modifications were available as candidates. An absent correct sequence cannot win a closed search. Conversely, adding many candidates can create additional competing explanations. Fixed modifications apply a specified change wherever the rule requires it; variable modifications generate alternatives at allowed sites. Neither setting proves that the chemistry happened. Constructed search-space exercise: a peptide has four eligible sites and each can independently be unmodified or carry one chosen modification. Without other constraints, it has 2⁴ = 16 positional states. Allowing at most one modified site leaves 1 + 4 = 5 . This counts candidates, not measured forms or equally likely biological states. Software may impose additional limits, and isobaric alternatives can still need distinguishing fragments. A PSM is a proposed relationship A PSM connects a spectrum to a candidate peptide interpretation, including relevant modifications and charge. Retain the spectrum identifier, candidate, score, mass error, and acceptance status. A spectrum can contain coisolated species; a single top-ranked assignment need not explain every peak. Inspect competing candidates and diagnostic fragments when a consequential claim depends on one spectrum. Search scores can be transformed into calibrated confidence estimates using additional modeling. PeptideProphet demonstrated a statistical model that distinguishes correct and incorrect assignments and estimates assignment probabilities. Such a modeled probability is a different object from an uncalibrated search score, and its validity depends on the model and data. [2] Name the error level and denominator Target–decoy analysis estimates incorrect assignments using deliberately constructed alternative sequences. Record decoy construction, competition, filtering, and whether discoveries are spectra, peptide sequences, modified peptide forms, or proteins. A nominal threshold and an estimated error rate are not the unknowable realized error fraction of a particular list. Read false discovery rate for the formal distinction. [3] Constructed known-truth example: 100 accepted PSMs contain 99 correct matches to the same peptide and one incorrect match to a different peptide. The realized PSM error fraction is 1/100 = 1% . Collapsing this list to two peptide sequences gives one false sequence out of two, or 50%. This artificial example is not an estimator. It proves that counting at one level does not automatically control another. Repeated evidence, cross-run combination, or a selected subgroup can change the relevant counting problem. A modified-peptide subset should not inherit a claimed subgroup error rate solely from the full search. Localization error and false discoveries in abundance comparisons are additional questions. Keep their procedures and thresholds distinct. Shared peptides create genuine ambiguity Constructed mapping example: protein A contains peptides p and q; protein B contains p and r. If only p is confidently observed, the evidence is compatible with A alone, B alone, or both. Repeating p twenty times improves evidence for that peptide but does not add a distinguishing sequence. If q is also observed and uniquely maps to A within the searched database, A receives distinguishing support; B still cannot be ruled out merely because r was not detected. Protein inference combines such mappings with confidence and inference rules. ProteinProphet is a foundational probabilistic method that handles peptides mapping to multiple proteins and derives a supported protein list. A parsimonious explanation aims to explain evidence with fewer proteins; that preference is not direct evidence that every additional compatible protein is absent. [4] Read a protein group before reading its name Software can group proteins whose evidence does not distinguish them and choose a leading or representative accession for display. The mzIdentML reporting framework explicitly distinguishes these roles. A representative label can be a reporting choice, rather than proof that this exact sequence was measured independently. Preserve group membership and distinguish supporting shared peptides from distinguishing peptides. [5] “Unique” also needs a reference: unique to a database accession, gene, or protein group are different claims. Check database release and isoform inclusion. Shared-peptide assignment for quantification is another explicit rule; assigning an intensity to one displayed protein does not retroactively make the peptide unique. The standard's links among spectra, peptide evidence, and database sequences make these decisions inspectable. [6] Coverage measures mapped sequence positions Sequence coverage is commonly the fraction of reference residue positions covered by accepted mapped peptides. State the reference, mapping and filtering rules. Constructed example: on a 100-residue sequence, peptides covering positions 1–10 and 6–15 cover 15 distinct residues, not 20. Coverage is 15%. Observing either peptide again does not add positions. High coverage does not alone resolve homologs if the covered regions are shared. Low coverage is not automatically a false identification if the evidence is strong and appropriate error control is used. Coverage also does not say which distant modifications coexist on the same intact molecule. For modified sequence reporting, ProForma provides explicit representations, including ambiguity; notation records a claim, not its experimental validation. [7] Check your understanding Can twenty PSMs establish two proteins that share the same observed peptide? No. Repeated measurement of the shared sequence does not distinguish its parents. Seek distinguishing sequence evidence or retain a protein-group interpretation. What makes an identification table reviewable? Explicit reporting units, database and search settings, confidence procedures, protein-group membership, and links back to spectra. Inspect modification positions separately in the PTM localization Guide.

title: 肽段鉴定与蛋白质推断
summary: 通过明确的教学例子区分分数、错误层级、共享肽段映射、蛋白质分组和序列覆盖率。
text: 把四个问题分开 肽段鉴定问的是：哪个候选能解释测得的证据？蛋白质推断问的是：已鉴定肽段支持哪些母体蛋白质？置信度估计问的是：在明确的程序下，通过筛选的结果有多大比例会出错？修饰定位问的是：哪个残基携带修饰？这些问题相互联系，但答好其中一个并不会自动答好其他问题。 从 碎片离子证据 和 自下而上工作流程 开始。本指南以传统的、以谱图为中心的数据库检索作为教学模型。DIA 和谱库流程可能采用不同的证据组织方式；请通过 采集指南 了解数据如何获得，并检查具体分析实际使用的报告单位。 检索结果取决于候选集合 数据库检索根据序列数据库、酶切规则、质量容差和修饰模型枚举候选肽段，再将预期碎片证据与测得的 MS/MS 谱图比较。SEQUEST 的互相关方法是评分函数的一个历史性例子，其数值尺度属于该方法。分数更高表示按该函数计算的一致性更强，并不代表普遍适用的正确概率。 [1] 检查候选集合是否包含目标物种、变体、常见污染物和相关修饰。如果正确序列根本不存在，它就不可能在封闭式检索中胜出。反过来，增加候选可能带来更多竞争解释。固定修饰在规则要求的位置施加指定变化；可变修饰在允许位点生成不同可能。任何一种设置都不能证明相应化学变化实际发生。 构造的检索空间练习： 某肽段有四个可修饰位点，每个位点都可以独立地保持未修饰或带一种指定修饰。没有其他约束时，共有 2⁴ = 16 种位置状态。若至多允许一个修饰位点，则剩下 1 + 4 = 5 种。这里数的是候选，不是实测形式，也不是等概率的生物学状态。软件可能施加额外限制，而等质量候选仍可能需要区分性碎片。 PSM 是一种待评估的对应关系 PSM 将谱图与一个候选肽段解释相联系，包括相关修饰和电荷。保留谱图标识、候选、分数、质量误差以及是否通过筛选的状态。谱图可能含有共同隔离的物种；单个最高排名指认不一定解释所有峰。如果重要陈述依赖单张谱图，应检查竞争候选和诊断性碎片。 通过额外建模，可以将检索分数转化为经过校准的置信度估计。PeptideProphet 展示了区分正确与错误指认并估计指认概率的统计模型。这种模型概率与未经校准的检索分数是不同对象，其有效性依赖于模型与数据。 [2] 写明错误层级和分母 目标–诱饵分析利用刻意构建的替代序列估计错误指认。记录诱饵构建、竞争、筛选方式，以及发现单位究竟是谱图、肽段序列、修饰肽形式，还是蛋白质。名义阈值和估计错误率，都不等于某个具体列表中未知的实际错误比例。请阅读 错误发现率 了解正式区别。 [3] 构造的已知真值例子： 100 条通过筛选的 PSM 中，99 条正确匹配同一肽段，另一条错误匹配另一个肽段。实际 PSM 错误比例是 1/100 = 1% 。把列表折叠为两个肽段序列后，其中一个序列错误，比例就是 50%。这个人工例子不是估计器；它证明，一个层级的计数不能自动控制另一个层级。 重复证据、跨运行合并或选择某个子集，都可能改变相关的计数问题。不能仅凭全体检索的错误控制，就声称修饰肽子集拥有同样的子集错误率。定位错误以及丰度比较中的错误发现是另外的问题，应保留各自的程序和阈值。 共享肽段带来真实的歧义 构造的映射例子： 蛋白质 A 含肽段 p 和 q；蛋白质 B 含 p 和 r。如果只可信地观察到 p，证据同时容许“只有 A”“只有 B”或“两者都有”。重复测得 p 二十次能加强该肽段的证据，却不会增加具有区分力的序列。如果还观察到 q，且它在所检索数据库中唯一映射到 A，那么 A 获得区分性支持；但仅因没有检测到 r，仍不能排除 B。 蛋白质推断 把这类映射与置信度及推断规则结合起来。ProteinProphet 是一种基础性的概率方法，处理可映射到多个蛋白质的肽段，并导出受到支持的蛋白质列表。简约解释希望用更少的蛋白质解释证据；这种偏好并不是其他兼容蛋白质均不存在的直接证据。 [4] 先读分组，再读名称 软件可以将证据无法区分的蛋白质归为一组，并选择领先或代表性登录号用于显示。mzIdentML 的报告框架明确区分这些角色。代表标签可能是一项报告选择，而不是该精确序列得到独立测量的证明。保留组内成员，并区分提供支持的共享肽段与具有区分力的肽段。 [5] “唯一”也需要参照：对于数据库登录号、基因或蛋白质分组唯一，是不同的陈述。检查数据库版本和是否包含异构体。定量时共享肽段的分配是另一条显式规则；把强度分给某个显示的蛋白质，不会倒过来让该肽段变得唯一。标准中谱图、肽段证据和数据库序列之间的联系，使这些决定能够被检查。 [6] 覆盖率计算被映射的序列位置 序列覆盖率 通常是通过筛选并完成映射的肽段所覆盖的参考残基位置比例。应写明参考序列、映射和筛选规则。 构造的例子： 在 100 个残基的序列上，分别覆盖位置 1–10 和 6–15 的肽段共覆盖 15 个不同残基，而不是 20 个。覆盖率是 15%。重复观察其中任一个肽段都不会增加被覆盖位置。 如果覆盖区域是共有的，高覆盖率也不能单独区分同源蛋白。若证据强且错误控制适当，低覆盖率也不自动等于错误鉴定。覆盖率还不能说明距离较远的修饰是否共存于同一完整分子上。ProForma 为修饰序列报告提供明确表示，包括歧义表示；符号记录的是一项陈述，并不等于实验验证。 [7] 检查你的理解 二十条 PSM 能确定含有同一个已观测共享肽段的两个蛋白质都存在吗？ 不能。重复测量共享序列无法区分其母体。应寻找有区分力的序列证据，或者保留蛋白质分组层面的解释。 什么让鉴定表格便于复核？ 明确的报告单位、数据库和检索设置、置信度程序、蛋白质分组成员以及返回谱图的联系。在 PTM 定位指南中，还要单独检查修饰位置。

title: PTM analysis and site localization
summary: Distinguish mass changes, modified peptides, localized sites, and occupancy with charge-aware and positional examples.
text: A modified peptide is not yet a localized site A post-translational modification changes a protein after translation. In a mass-spectrometric workflow, a measured mass shift can also arise from deliberate preparation chemistry or an artifact. Distinguish the observed mass change, the proposed chemical modification, its position, and its biological origin. ProForma explicitly accommodates natural, chemically induced, and artifactual modifications in sequence descriptions. [1] This Guide focuses on bottom-up modification analysis, using phosphorylation as a teaching example. Begin with peptide identification and protein inference . Identifying the peptide backbone, identifying a modification type, and localizing its site require different evidence. A protein name with a residue number can hide uncertainty at all three stages. Begin with a chemical hypothesis Unimod records phosphorylation with a monoisotopic mass increment of 79.966331 Da . For the same ion composition and unchanged charge of +2, one such increment shifts m/z by approximately 79.966331 / 2 = 39.983166 . This charge-aware arithmetic supports candidate generation; a matching precursor shift alone does not identify the residue or exclude another composition within the measurement tolerance. [2] Specify which residues and termini can carry each searched change, whether it is fixed or variable, and the permitted number per peptide. Constraining the search to familiar sites can exclude real alternatives, while opening every possibility increases competition. A search setting describes allowed explanations, not biological proof. Keep unexpected mass shifts separate from fully characterized chemical identities. Enrichment changes the measured population Modified peptides can require enrichment before LC-MS/MS. Phosphopeptide methods include immobilized metal-ion affinity and metal-oxide approaches; antibodies or other affinity reagents address other selected chemistries. Primary comparisons of phosphopeptide enrichment show overlapping but distinct selectivity among conditions and materials. An enrichment method therefore defines a sampling preference, not an unbiased inventory of every modification. [3] Record input amount, preparation, enrichment chemistry, and recovered fractions. Compare suitable controls and retain an unenriched aliquot when the question requires information about total protein abundance. A missing enriched signal can reflect low abundance, loss, poor binding, or failed measurement. It does not by itself demonstrate that a site was unmodified in the original sample. Ask which fragments distinguish positions Two peptide forms can have the same sequence and precursor mass while placing the same modification at different residues. Fragments containing both candidate sites, or neither, may be identical under those alternatives. Site localization depends on evidence that distinguishes the competing placements. Ascore's foundational approach used site-determining ions; total spectral agreement and positional discrimination are different requirements. [4] Constructed positional example: consider ASSTK with exactly one phosphate, allowing only S2 or S3. Assume b/y backbone fragments retain the modification and have charge +1. The b2 fragment contains A1–S2, so phosphorylation at S2 shifts b2 while phosphorylation at S3 does not. The y3 fragment contains S3–T4–K5 and has the opposite distinction. In contrast, b3 contains both candidate serines and carries one phosphate under either placement. If only b3 and the precursor are observed, this simplified evidence does not distinguish S2 from S3. Adding credible b2 or y3 evidence can help, but a real analysis must evaluate mass tolerance, intensity, interference, and alternative explanations. These are theoretical fragment relationships, not a synthetic experimental spectrum or a guarantee that any fragment will be detectable. Match activation to the evidence needed Labile groups can be lost during activation, and a neutral-loss signal alone usually does not identify the modified residue. Fragmentation methods produce different evidence depending on peptide charge, sequence, modification chemistry, and instrument conditions. ETD demonstrated sequence analysis with preservation of labile modifications in suitable peptide ions. That capability is not a promise of complete localization for every modified peptide. [5] Use the fragmentation Guide to connect activation and product-ion interpretation, and the acquisition Guide for measurement scheduling. Choose evidence needed to separate candidate sites rather than choosing a method solely by its label. Identification and localization have separate errors An accepted peptide assignment can still carry a wrongly placed modification. Conversely, an apparently decisive positional score is not trustworthy if the peptide identity is wrong. State the identification threshold, localization method, candidate sites, score interpretation, and aggregation level. PTMProphet models site probabilities and estimates false localization rates; these quantities concern positional assignments and should not be relabeled as peptide-identification FDR. [6] Constructed conditional example: suppose 100 accepted spectra all have the correct peptide sequence and modification count, but ten have the wrong assigned site. Their realized peptide-assignment error fraction is zero and their site-assignment error fraction is 10%. This known-truth illustration does not estimate either rate from unknown data. Repeated spectra and multiply modified peptides require an explicitly defined unit before counting localization errors. Abundance change is not absolute occupancy Modification occupancy is the fraction of eligible molecules modified at a specified site. A modified-peptide intensity can change because total protein amount changes, occupancy changes, or measurement response changes. Absolute occupancy requires additional information and a validated model; raw intensities of modified and unmodified forms need not have equal response factors. Dedicated phosphorylation-stoichiometry methods demonstrate this distinction. [7] Constructed amount example: a sample contains 100 amount units of protein at 20% site occupancy, giving 20 modified units. A second sample contains 200 total units at the same occupancy, giving 40 modified units. The modified amount doubles without any occupancy increase. Even after suitable protein-level correction, a relative occupancy change does not automatically establish the absolute occupancy in either sample. Preserve uncertainty through reporting Report accession and sequence version, peptide-to-protein mapping, residue numbering, modification identifier, candidate positions, and localization evidence. A confidently localized peptide site can map to several protein accessions. Preserve that ambiguity instead of assigning an unsupported isoform-specific site. Unimod's oxidation record also illustrates why a modification name alone does not establish whether it arose biologically or during handling. [8] Check your understanding Does a phosphate-like precursor shift locate phosphorylation? No. It supports a mass-change hypothesis. Distinguishing positions requires appropriate evidence, and establishing biological origin requires additional context. Does twice the modified signal mean twice the occupancy? No. Check total protein abundance, recovery, enrichment, response, and localization first. State whether the reported result is signal, modified amount, relative occupancy change, or absolute occupancy.

title: 翻译后修饰分析与位点定位
summary: 通过考虑电荷和修饰位置的例子，区分质量变化、修饰肽段、已定位位点和占有率。
text: 鉴定修饰肽段不等于定位修饰位点 翻译后修饰 是在翻译之后发生的蛋白质变化。在质谱流程中，测得的质量偏移也可能来自有意的制备化学处理或伪影。应区分观察到的质量变化、提出的化学修饰、其位置和生物学来源。ProForma 在序列描述中明确容纳天然、化学引入和伪影性修饰。 [1] 本指南聚焦自下而上的修饰分析，以磷酸化作为教学例子。先阅读 肽段鉴定与蛋白质推断 。鉴定肽段骨架、确定修饰类型和定位修饰位点，需要不同的证据。一个附有残基编号的蛋白质名称，可能掩盖这三个阶段的全部不确定性。 从化学假设开始 Unimod 将磷酸化的单同位素质量增量记为 79.966331 Da 。在离子组成的其他部分相同且电荷保持 +2 时，一个这样的增量使 m/z 移动约 79.966331 / 2 = 39.983166 。这一考虑电荷的算术支持候选生成；仅有吻合的前体偏移，既不能确定残基，也不能排除测量容差内的其他组成。 [2] 说明每种检索变化允许出现在哪些残基和末端，是固定还是可变，以及每个肽段允许多少处。只允许熟悉的位点可能排除真实的其他位置，而把所有可能都开放则会增加竞争。检索设置描述允许的解释，并不是生物学证明。应将意外质量偏移与已充分表征的化学身份分开。 富集改变被测群体 修饰肽段在 LC-MS/MS 前可能需要富集。磷酸肽方法包括固定化金属离子亲和及金属氧化物路线；抗体或其他亲和试剂则针对其他特定化学类型。磷酸肽富集的原始比较研究显示，不同条件与材料的选择性既有重叠，也有差异。因此，富集方法定义了采样偏好，并不是对所有修饰无偏的清单。 [3] 记录输入量、制备、富集化学及回收组分。比较合适的对照；当问题需要总蛋白丰度信息时，保留未富集的等分样本。富集信号缺失可能来自低丰度、损失、结合不良或测量失败，本身不能证明原始样本中的该位点未被修饰。 问哪些碎片能区分位置 两种肽段形式可以有相同序列和前体质量，却把同一修饰放在不同残基上。在这些候选下，包含两个候选位点或一个也不包含的碎片可能完全相同。 位点定位 依赖于能够区分竞争位置的证据。Ascore 的基础方法使用决定位置的离子；整体谱图一致性与位置区分力是不同要求。 [4] 构造的位置例子： 考虑 ASSTK ，恰有一个磷酸基，且仅允许位于 S2 或 S3。假设 b/y 骨架碎片保留修饰，电荷均为 +1。b2 碎片含 A1–S2，所以 S2 磷酸化会使 b2 偏移，而 S3 磷酸化不会。y3 碎片含 S3–T4–K5，其区分关系正好相反。相比之下，b3 含两个候选丝氨酸，在两种位置安排下都携带一个磷酸基。 若只观察到 b3 和前体，这组简化证据无法区分 S2 与 S3。加入可信的 b2 或 y3 证据会有帮助，但真实分析还必须评估质量容差、强度、干扰和其他解释。这里描述的是理论碎片关系，不是合成的实验谱图，也不保证任何碎片都能被检测到。 让活化方式服务于所需证据 不稳定基团可能在活化中丢失，而单独的中性丢失信号通常不能确定被修饰残基。碎裂方法产生的证据取决于肽段电荷、序列、修饰化学和仪器条件。ETD 曾在适合的肽段离子中展示保留不稳定修饰的序列分析能力。这并不保证每个修饰肽段都能被完整定位。 [5] 通过 碎裂指南 将活化与产物离子解释联系起来，通过 采集指南 了解测量安排。应根据区分候选位点需要什么证据来选择，而不是仅凭方法名称做决定。 鉴定和定位各有错误 通过筛选的肽段指认仍可能把修饰放错位置。反过来，如果肽段身份本身错误，看似明确的位置分数也不可信。写明鉴定阈值、定位方法、候选位点、分数含义和汇总层级。PTMProphet 对位点概率建模并估计错误定位率；这些量针对位置指认，不应被改称为肽段鉴定 FDR。 [6] 构造的条件例子： 假设 100 张通过筛选的谱图都具有正确的肽段序列和修饰数目，但其中十张的位点指认错误。其实际肽段指认错误比例为零，位点指认错误比例却为 10%。这个已知真值例子不能从未知数据中估计任何一种错误率。重复谱图和多重修饰肽段在统计定位错误之前，都需要先明确定义计数单位。 丰度变化不等于绝对占有率 修饰占有率是可接受该修饰的分子中，某指定位点被修饰的比例。修饰肽强度可能因总蛋白量、占有率或测量响应变化而改变。绝对占有率需要额外信息和经过验证的模型；修饰与未修饰形式的原始强度并不一定具有相同响应因子。专门的磷酸化化学计量方法展示了这一区别。 [7] 构造的物质量例子： 一份样本含 100 单位蛋白质，位点占有率为 20%，因此有 20 个修饰单位。第二份样本含 200 个总单位，占有率相同，因此有 40 个修饰单位。修饰量翻倍，而占有率没有上升。即使经过合适的蛋白质层面校正，相对占有率变化也不能自动给出任一份样本的绝对占有率。 报告时保留不确定性 报告登录号和序列版本、肽段–蛋白质映射、残基编号、修饰标识、候选位置及定位证据。可信定位的肽段位点仍可能映射到多个蛋白质登录号。应保留这种歧义，而不是给出缺乏支持的异构体特异位点。Unimod 的氧化记录也说明，仅有修饰名称并不能确定它来自生物过程还是样本处理。 [8] 检查你的理解 与磷酸基相符的前体偏移能定位磷酸化吗？ 不能。它支持质量变化假设。区分位置需要合适的证据，确定生物学来源则需要更多背景。 修饰信号翻倍就表示占有率翻倍吗？ 不能。先检查总蛋白丰度、回收、富集、响应和定位。说明报告的是信号、修饰量、相对占有率变化，还是绝对占有率。

title: Small-molecule annotation: from features to identity
summary: Build ion, formula, and structure hypotheses, compare reference evidence, and report what remains unresolved.
text: Annotate the evidence before naming the molecule A small-molecule annotation is a proposed relationship between a measured signal and a chemical explanation. The explanation may be an ion form, a molecular formula, a compound class, or a particular structure. These are different claims. A workflow should preserve the strongest defensible claim without filling unresolved details with a familiar database name. This Guide develops the identity layer introduced in data analysis ; all numerical observations below are constructed teaching examples. Start with a question that can be tested: “Does this feature support this candidate under these measurement conditions?” Replacing that question with “What is the first database hit?” hides both alternative candidates and the limitations of the measurement. First establish what the signal represents Inspect the underlying chromatographic trace, isotope envelope, blanks, and MS/MS scan rather than trusting a result-table row alone. An adduct ion , an isotopologue , and an in-source product can generate different features from the same compound. Conversely, unresolved compounds can contribute to one feature. Keep feature evidence separate from molecule summaries, as the mzTab-M results model does. [1] Record polarity, charge, proposed adduct, monoisotopic-peak choice, retention time, and the isolation window. For mixed spectra, ask which product ions actually follow the selected precursor. A fragment observed in the same scan is not automatically evidence for every coisolated candidate. Reacquisition with a narrower window or an altered separation may test the association. Build a formula hypothesis with explicit assumptions A molecular formula specifies atom counts, not their connectivity. Convert the proposed ion form to the appropriate neutral composition before searching. Restrict elements only when justified by the sample and experiment; a carbon/hydrogen/oxygen-only search cannot discover a nitrogen-containing answer. Isotope information, chemically plausible element ratios, and valence rules can narrow the list. Heuristic filters are prioritization tools, not guarantees that an excluded unfamiliar compound cannot exist. [2] Constructed calculation: assume a singly protonated ion, [M+H] + , of neutral C 6 H 12 O 6 , using 12 C, 1 H, and 16 O. Its calculated monoisotopic neutral mass is 180.063388 Da and calculated m/z is 181.070665 after rounding. These values use the linked atomic masses and proton mass. [3] [4] [5] [6] If observed m/z is 181.070846, the signed error relative to the rounded theoretical coordinate is (181.070846 − 181.070665)/181.070665 × 10 6 = +1.00 ppm. A ±5 ppm search accepts that match; its half-width here is approximately 0.000905 m/z. Acceptance means the observation is compatible with this hypothesis under that tolerance. It neither proves a unique formula nor distinguishes the structures sharing the formula. Reassigning the peak as a sodium adduct would require a different mass correction and a new candidate search. Use a spectral library as a comparison experiment A spectral library contains reference spectra and associated metadata. MassBank records, for example, connect spectral data with chemical and experimental information. [7] Choose references compatible with the ionization method, polarity, precursor form, fragmentation method, and collision conditions. An EI spectrum is not an interchangeable reference for an ESI tandem spectrum. Examine the matched peaks, their relative intensities, unmatched substantial peaks, and whether the candidate explains the chemically informative fragments. Preserve the accession, library version, score definition, preprocessing, mass tolerances, and candidate list. A score of 0.95 is a number on an algorithm's scale; it is not automatically a 95% probability of correct identification. A high score based mostly on a common fragment may distinguish a class poorly, and the correct candidate may be absent from the library. State confidence and structural specificity separately The MSI chemical-analysis recommendations distinguish identified compounds, putatively annotated compounds, putatively characterized classes, and unknowns. For a previously known metabolite, their level-1 proposal calls for at least two independent, orthogonal properties matched to an authentic compound analyzed under identical conditions. A literature or external-library match alone does not meet that proposal. [8] Name the confidence framework and the evidence used rather than reporting an unexplained level number. Also state structural specificity: a formula, connectivity assignment, and stereochemical assignment are not equivalent. Comparing a standard's retention time and MS/MS can strengthen a claim, but the method must actually distinguish the relevant alternatives. Two enantiomers may remain indistinguishable in an achiral workflow. More digits in m/z do not supply missing stereochemical evidence. Turn competing candidates into the next experiment Suppose the constructed C 6 H 12 O 6 feature has two plausible isomer candidates, A and B. Both pass the mass filter and share the dominant MS/MS products. A library ranks A first, but B has no spectrum at the acquired collision energy. The honest result is a candidate annotation with unresolved isomerism, not exclusion of B. Next, measure authentic A and B using the sample's chromatographic and MS/MS method. If both standards coelute and remain spectrally indistinguishable, the extra measurements have exposed a method limitation. If they separate reproducibly and the sample matches A under validated matching criteria, the assignment becomes more specific. If the sample contains both peaks, report both supported components; do not compress the mixture into the original single name. Choose follow-up measurements for their ability to discriminate the remaining candidates. Make uncertainty reusable A useful record includes a stable feature identifier; measured coordinates; ion assignment; formula and structure candidates; supporting spectra and standards; confidence framework; unresolved alternatives; and the reason for accepting or rejecting each important claim. Retain unknowns with traceable signals. They can become interpretable when a reference is added without pretending that an annotation was already established. Check your understanding A formula is unique within the search settings. Is the compound identified? No. The settings may omit the correct formula, and even the correct formula can describe several isomers. Inspect the settings and add evidence that distinguishes structures. Beyond the basics Continue with lipid structural evidence for naming claims at different structural depths, or ion mobility and CCS for another measurable constraint. Additional measurements are useful when they test an uncertainty, not merely when they add another score.

title: 小分子注释：从特征到身份
summary: 建立离子、分子式和结构假设，比较参考证据，并报告尚未解决的问题。
text: 先注释证据，再给分子命名 小分子注释是对测量信号与化学解释之间关系的提议。这个解释可能是离子形式、分子式、化合物类别或某个特定结构。这些是不同层次的主张。工作流程应保留证据能够支持的最强结论，而不是用熟悉的数据库名称填补未解决的细节。本指南进一步展开 数据分析 中的身份判定环节；以下所有数值观测均为构造的教学示例。 从一个可以检验的问题出发：“在这些测量条件下，该特征是否支持这个候选物？”若把它替换成“数据库的第一条命中是什么？”，就会掩盖其他候选物及测量本身的局限。 先确定信号代表什么 检查原始色谱轨迹、同位素包络、空白和 MS/MS 扫描，不要只相信结果表中的一行。 加合离子 、 同位素体 以及源内产物，可以使同一个化合物形成不同特征。反过来，未分开的化合物也可能共同贡献一个特征。应像 mzTab-M 结果模型那样，将特征证据与分子汇总分开保存。 [1] 记录极性、电荷、所提议的加合形式、单同位素峰选择、保留时间和隔离窗口。遇到混合谱时，要问哪些产物离子真正跟随选定前体变化。同一次扫描中观察到的碎片，不会自动成为每个共隔离候选物的证据。缩窄隔离窗口或改变分离条件后重新采集，有助于检验这种归属。 在明确假设下提出分子式 分子式 给出原子数目，而非原子连接关系。检索前，应把提议的离子形式正确换算为中性组成。只有样品和实验提供依据时才能限制元素范围；仅搜索碳、氢、氧，不可能找到含氮的答案。同位素信息、化学上合理的元素比例和价态规则可以缩小候选范围。启发式筛选是排序工具，并不保证被排除的陌生化合物一定不存在。 [2] 构造计算： 假设中性 C 6 H 12 O 6 形成单质子化离子 [M+H] + ，计算采用 12 C、 1 H 和 16 O。舍入后，中性分子的单同位素质量为 180.063388 Da，离子的理论 m/z 为 181.070665。这些数值使用所链接的原子质量和质子质量。 [3] [4] [5] [6] 若实测 m/z 为 181.070846，相对于已舍入理论坐标的带符号误差为 (181.070846 − 181.070665)/181.070665 × 10 6 = +1.00 ppm。±5 ppm 的检索会接受该匹配；在这里，其半窗口宽度约为 0.000905 m/z。接受匹配只表示：在该容差下，观测与这一假设相容。它既不能证明分子式唯一，也不能区分共享该分子式的不同结构。若改判为钠加合离子，就必须采用另一种质量修正，并重新搜索候选物。 把谱库视为比较实验 谱库 包含参考谱及相关元数据。例如，MassBank 记录把谱数据与化学和实验信息联系起来。 [7] 选择与电离方式、极性、前体形式、碎裂方法和碰撞条件相容的参考谱。EI 谱不能直接替代 ESI 串联质谱的参考谱。 检查匹配峰、相对强度、未匹配的重要峰，以及候选物能否解释具有化学信息的碎片。保存记录编号、谱库版本、评分定义、预处理、质量容差和候选列表。0.95 的分数只是某个算法尺度上的数值，并不自动等于身份正确的概率为 95%。若高分主要来自一个常见碎片，可能连类别也难以区分；正确候选物还可能根本不在谱库中。 分别说明置信程度和结构细节 MSI 化学分析建议区分已鉴定化合物、推定注释化合物、推定表征类别和未知物。对于已知代谢物，其一级鉴定建议要求：至少两项相互独立、正交的性质，与在相同实验条件下分析的真实标准品相匹配。仅与文献或外部谱库匹配，达不到这一建议的要求。 [8] 应说明采用的置信分级体系和证据，而不是只给出没有解释的等级数字。同时说明结构具体程度：分子式、连接关系和立体化学归属并不等价。比较标准品的保留时间和 MS/MS 可增强结论，但方法必须确实能够区分相关替代结构。在非手性流程中，两个对映异构体可能仍无法区分。增加 m/z 的小数位数，不能补上缺失的立体化学证据。 用竞争候选物决定下一步实验 假设上述构造的 C 6 H 12 O 6 特征有两个合理的异构体候选物 A 和 B。两者都通过质量筛选，并共享主要 MS/MS 产物。谱库把 A 排在首位，但没有 B 在当前碰撞能量下的谱图。诚实的结果应是异构体尚未区分的候选注释，而不是宣称已经排除 B。 下一步，用样品的色谱和 MS/MS 方法测量真实的 A、B 标准品。如果两个标准品共洗脱，且谱图仍无法区分，新增实验揭示的是方法局限。如果两者可重复地分开，且样品在经验证的匹配判据下与 A 一致，归属就变得更具体。如果样品同时含有两个峰，应报告各自受到支持的组分，不要把混合物压缩为最初的一个名称。应根据能否区分剩余候选物来选择后续测量。 让不确定性可以复用 有用的记录包括稳定的特征标识符、测量坐标、离子归属、分子式和结构候选、支持谱图和标准品、置信体系、未解决的替代解释，以及接受或否定每项重要主张的原因。保留能够追溯信号的未知物。将来增加参考数据后，它们可能变得可解释，无须假装现在就已建立注释。 检查你的理解 在当前检索设置中只有一个分子式，是否就鉴定了化合物？ 不是。检索设置可能遗漏正确分子式；即使分子式正确，也可能对应多个异构体。应检查设置，并增加能够区分结构的证据。 进一步学习 继续阅读 脂质结构证据 ，了解不同结构深度的命名；或阅读 离子淌度与 CCS ，了解另一种可测量的约束。新增测量的价值在于检验不确定性，而不只是增加一个分数。

title: Lipidomics: match structural detail to evidence
summary: Distinguish lipid class, sum composition, chains, sn positions, and double-bond evidence without overnaming a signal.
text: A lipid name is a set of structural claims Lipidomics measures chemically diverse lipids, often in mixtures where many candidates have related masses and fragments. A reported lipid name should reveal which structural details the experiment established. Class, total chain composition, individual chains, chain positions, double-bond positions, and stereochemistry require different evidence. A longer name is not automatically a better result. This Guide explains structural interpretation, not disease associations or a ranking of instruments. The LIPID MAPS shorthand system encodes a hierarchy of structural information. Its punctuation helps preserve uncertainty rather than forcing every measurement into a fully drawn molecule. [1] The terminology entry provides a compact reminder; below, all candidate sets and measurement scenarios are constructed teaching examples. Read the information actually encoded Class and sum composition: PC 34:1 reports phosphatidylcholine with a total of 34 chain carbons and one chain unsaturation equivalent in this simple, unmodified diacyl-PC example. The headgroup and glycerol carbons are not included in 34. Chain composition: PC 16:0_18:1 reports the two chains while leaving their glycerol sn positions unresolved. The underscore is deliberate. Chain positions: PC 16:0/18:1 assigns 16:0 to sn-1 and 18:1 to sn-2; the slash makes a stronger claim. Double-bond detail: PC 16:0/18:1(9Z) additionally assigns a double bond at carbon 9 of the 18-carbon chain and its Z geometry. These examples assume the stated diacyl backbone. Ether linkages, additional oxygens, rings, and other modifications require the corresponding notation rules. More generally, the count after the colon can represent double-bond equivalents; do not silently interpret every unsaturation as an experimentally localized carbon–carbon double bond. The official nomenclature resource links the full rules and application examples. [2] Establish the precursor and class context Identify polarity, charge, and adduct before comparing a mass with a lipid database. The same neutral lipid can produce different ion forms, and different classes may yield isomeric or nearby precursor signals. Accurate mass is a useful filter, but a database's plausible formula is not independent evidence for the assigned class. Check which class-indicating fragments or losses the actual precursor form produces. A commonly observed phosphocholine product near m/z 184.073 in positive mode is shared by phosphatidylcholines and sphingomyelins; it is not a unique identifier of one PC molecular species. [3] Interpret such evidence with precursor composition, other products, and separation context. The Lipidomics Standards Initiative asks for documented ion forms, diagnostic fragments, standards, and checks for background and isomer overlap. [4] Do chain fragments belong to the same lipid? Appropriate MS/MS experiments can reveal acyl-chain information beyond a class fragment, but fragment production depends on class, adduct, polarity, and activation. LSI distinguishes sum-composition measurements from methods supporting chain and positional assignments. [5] Do not assume that every positive-mode spectrum reports both chains, or that the most intense chain-related product universally marks sn-2. In a mixture, an isolation window can contain several lipids. A spectrum containing evidence for 16:0, 18:1, 16:1, and 18:0 is not permission to attach all four chains to one diacyl PC. Inspect coelution, precursor purity, isotope overlap, and whether products track the same chromatographic or mobility component. Any rule that assigns sn positions from intensity ratios needs validation for the class and acquisition conditions used. Worked example: the same total, different structures Consider three candidate chain compositions: PC 16:0_18:1, PC 16:1_18:0, and PC 14:0_20:1. Each satisfies 16+18 = 34 or 14+20 = 34 carbons, and each has 0+1 = 1 unsaturation. Therefore all are compatible with PC 34:1 under the stated diacyl assumptions. Their sum-composition arithmetic cannot distinguish them. Suppose clean, appropriately assigned chain evidence supports 16:0 and 18:1. Report PC 16:0_18:1. If there is no validated sn-position evidence, replacing the underscore with a slash invents information. If the 18:1 double-bond location is unresolved, keep 18:1 rather than naming a specific positional isomer. A database drawing that happens to show 9Z does not supply an experimental localization. Now suppose a second chromatographic component shares the sum composition but supports 16:1 and 18:0. Report separate feature-to-annotation links. An aggregate PC 34:1 quantity may still be useful for a specified purpose, but it describes the combined measured pool only if the integration and response model support that aggregation. It cannot establish that one particular isomer increased. Choose evidence for the missing structural dimension Double-bond-sensitive chemistry can produce position-diagnostic products. Ozone-induced dissociation reacts mass-selected lipid ions with ozone to reveal double-bond locations. [6] Paternò–Büchi derivatization followed by MS/MS is another route to location-sensitive fragments. [7] These methods answer a different question from ordinary sum-composition assignment; they do not automatically establish every chain position or stereochemical detail. Chromatography can provide independent discrimination, but similar retention is not a universal identity test. LSI recommends evaluating retention behavior and demonstrating relevant isomer separation with authentic standards or appropriate supporting models. [8] Compare standards under the actual method, and verify the alternatives are resolved before interpreting a match as specific. Report evidence and quantity at compatible levels For each annotation, record class, ion form, measured precursor, diagnostic products, separation evidence, standard use, software settings, and the structural level justified. Keep plausible alternatives and mixed components visible. The Lipidomics Minimal Reporting Checklist organizes identification, quantification, and quality information so results can be assessed and reused. [9] Identity confidence and quantitative validation remain separate. A well-supported structure can have an uncertain concentration; a reproducible sum-composition signal can remain an unresolved mixture. State whether the reported quantity belongs to a feature, a chain-defined species, or a pooled composition, and avoid using a class-level internal standard as evidence for a detailed structural assignment. Check your understanding Does observing 16:0 and 18:1 justify PC 16:0/18:1(9Z)? No. First establish that both chains belong to the same PC precursor. Their identities alone do not establish sn positions, double-bond location, or geometry. PC 16:0_18:1 preserves those unresolved details. Beyond the basics Use the annotation workflow to organize confidence and ion mobility to explore another separation dimension. Add structural detail only when the new experiment supports the corresponding claim.

title: 脂质组学：让结构细节与证据相匹配
summary: 区分脂质类别、总组成、链、sn 位置和双键证据，避免给信号赋予过度具体的名称。
text: 脂质名称包含一组结构主张 脂质组学测量结构多样的脂质，样品通常是混合物，其中许多候选物具有相近的质量和碎片。所报告的脂质名称应展示实验究竟建立了哪些结构细节。类别、链总组成、各条链、链位置、双键位置和立体化学需要不同证据。名称越长，并不自动意味着结果越好。本指南关注结构解释，不讨论疾病关联或仪器排名。 LIPID MAPS 简写体系编码了不同层次的结构信息。其中的标点有助于保留不确定性，而不是强迫每次测量都对应一幅完整结构图。 [1] 术语条目 提供简要说明；下文的候选集合和测量情境均为构造的教学示例。 读出名称真正编码的信息 类别和总组成： 在这个简单、未经修饰的二酰基 PC 示例中，PC 34:1 表示磷脂酰胆碱，两条链共有 34 个碳和一个链不饱和当量。34 不包括头基和甘油中的碳。 链组成： PC 16:0_18:1 表示两条链已知，但其在甘油上的 sn 位置尚未确定。下划线是有意保留的。 链位置： PC 16:0/18:1 将 16:0 归于 sn-1，将 18:1 归于 sn-2；斜线表达了更强的主张。 双键细节： PC 16:0/18:1(9Z) 进一步指定 18 碳链的第 9 位有双键，并指定其为 Z 构型。 这些示例假定所述二酰基骨架。醚键、额外氧原子、环及其他修饰需要相应的命名规则。更一般地说，冒号后面的数目可以表示双键当量；不要把所有不饱和度都默认为已由实验定位的碳碳双键。官方命名资源提供完整规则和应用示例的链接。 [2] 确定前体与类别背景 在把质量与脂质数据库比较前，先确定极性、电荷和 加合形式 。同一个中性脂质可以形成不同离子；不同类别也可能产生互为异构体或十分接近的前体信号。准确质量是有用的筛选条件，但数据库中的合理分子式不是类别归属的独立证据。 检查实际前体形式会产生哪些提示类别的碎片或丢失。在正离子模式下，m/z 184.073 附近常见的磷酸胆碱产物可由磷脂酰胆碱和鞘磷脂共同产生；它不是某一种 PC 分子种的唯一标识。 [3] 应结合前体组成、其他产物和分离背景解释此类证据。脂质组学标准倡议要求记录离子形式、诊断碎片、标准品，以及对背景和异构体重叠的检查。 [4] 链碎片是否属于同一个脂质？ 合适的 MS/MS 实验可以提供超出类别碎片的酰基链信息，但碎片产生取决于类别、加合形式、极性和活化方式。LSI 区分总组成测量与能够支持链及位置归属的方法。 [5] 不要假设每张正离子谱都能显示两条链，也不要假设最强的链相关产物总是代表 sn-2。 在混合物中，一个隔离窗口可能包含多个脂质。谱图中同时出现 16:0、18:1、16:1 和 18:0 的证据，并不意味着可以将四条链都赋给一个二酰基 PC。检查共洗脱、前体纯度、同位素重叠，以及产物是否跟随同一个色谱或淌度组分。任何根据强度比赋予 sn 位置的规则，都需要针对所用脂质类别和采集条件验证。 实例：相同总组成，不同结构 考虑三个候选链组成：PC 16:0_18:1、PC 16:1_18:0 和 PC 14:0_20:1。它们分别满足 16+18 = 34 或 14+20 = 34 个碳，且不饱和度均为 0+1 = 1。因此，在所述二酰基假设下，三者都与 PC 34:1 相容。总组成的算术无法区分它们。 假设干净且归属恰当的链证据支持 16:0 和 18:1，应报告 PC 16:0_18:1。若没有经过验证的 sn 位置证据，把下划线换成斜线就是添加不存在的信息。若 18:1 的双键位置未确定，应保留 18:1，而不要指定某个位置异构体。数据库结构图碰巧画成 9Z，并不能提供实验定位。 现在假设第二个色谱组分具有相同总组成，但支持 16:1 和 18:0。应分别保留特征与注释的对应关系。对于特定目的，汇总的 PC 34:1 定量仍可能有用，但只有积分和响应模型支持这种汇总时，它才描述合并测得的组分池。它不能证明某个特定异构体增加了。 针对缺失的结构维度选择证据 对双键敏感的化学过程可以产生定位诊断产物。臭氧诱导解离使质量选择后的脂质离子与臭氧反应，从而揭示双键位置。 [6] Paternò–Büchi 衍生化结合 MS/MS 是产生位置敏感碎片的另一条途径。 [7] 这些方法回答的问题不同于普通总组成归属；它们不会自动确定所有链位置或立体化学细节。 色谱可以提供独立区分，但相似保留时间不是通用的身份检验。LSI 建议评估保留行为，并用真实标准品或合适的支持模型证明相关异构体的分离。 [8] 应在实际方法下比较标准品，在把匹配解释为特异性结论前，确认替代结构确实被分开。 在相容层次上报告证据与定量 对每个注释，记录类别、离子形式、实测前体、诊断产物、分离证据、标准品使用情况、软件设置及有依据的结构层次。保留合理替代解释和混合组分。脂质组学最低报告清单组织了鉴定、定量和质量信息，使结果可以被评估和复用。 [9] 身份置信程度与定量验证仍是两回事。结构证据充分的脂质，其浓度仍可能不确定；可重复测得的总组成信号，也可能仍是未分开的混合物。说明所报告的量属于一个特征、链已确定的分子种，还是合并组成；不要用类别层面的内标来证明精细结构归属。 检查你的理解 观察到 16:0 和 18:1，就能报告 PC 16:0/18:1(9Z) 吗？ 不能。先要证明两条链属于同一个 PC 前体。仅有链身份，无法确定 sn 位置、双键位置或几何构型。PC 16:0_18:1 保留了这些尚未解决的细节。 进一步学习 用 小分子注释流程 组织置信证据，用 离子淌度 探索另一种分离维度。只有新实验支持相应主张时，才增加结构细节。

title: Ion mobility and collision cross section
summary: Separate measured mobility coordinates from derived CCS and compare ions with explicit gas, temperature, and calibration context.
text: Add a gas-phase separation coordinate Ion mobility separates gas-phase ions according to their motion through a gas under an electric field. Coupling it to MS adds information beyond m/z: ions with the same measured mass-to-charge ratio can have different mobilities. That extra coordinate can help separate interferences or constrain candidates, but it is not a direct photograph of a molecule. Distinguish the instrument's observed coordinate, a derived mobility, and a derived collision cross section. [1] This Guide introduces how to read those quantities and compare them responsibly. The worked values are deliberately constructed for arithmetic, not specifications or performance claims for a commercial instrument. From motion to mobility For an ideal uniform-field drift region with negligible bulk gas flow along the drift direction, drift velocity v d = KE. Here K is mobility and E is electric-field strength. If the effective drift length is L and the time within that region is t D , K = L/(Et D ). K can be expressed in m 2 V −1 s −1 or cm 2 V −1 s −1 . These equations require the appropriate drift time, not every recorded elapsed time. Reduced mobility K 0 corrects for gas number density using a stated reference: K 0 = K(N/N 0 ). Record the reference convention. Density normalization does not erase changes in gas composition, temperature-dependent collision behavior, or reduced field E/N. Reporting recommendations treat these as part of the measurement's definition. [1] Different instruments observe different coordinates Drift-tube IM: an electric field drives ions along a gas-filled region. Stepped-field measurements can separate the drift contribution from time outside that region; calibrated single-field workflows also exist. [2] Traveling-wave IM: moving electric potential waves transport ions. The relationship between arrival time and mobility is not the simple uniform-field formula above; wave conditions and an appropriate conversion procedure matter. [3] Trapped IM: an electric field counteracts gas flow, and ions are released as the field is scanned. The release coordinate is converted to mobility using the instrument model and calibration. [4] Differential mobility methods: separation uses differences in mobility at high and low fields. A compensation-voltage setting is not itself a conventional low-field CCS value. [5] Consequently, an axis labeled “mobility” may represent arrival time, inverse reduced mobility, or another coordinate. Read its units and metadata before comparing peaks across instruments. Do not apply a drift-tube equation to a trapped-ion release time or a traveling-wave transit time without the required model. Worked example: subtract the non-drift time Assume an ideal uniform field, L = 0.100 m, E = 10,000 V/m, and a measured arrival time of 52.0 ms. An independently established 2.0 ms belongs to transport outside the drift region. Therefore t D = 50.0 ms = 0.0500 s, and K = 0.100/(10,000 × 0.0500) = 0.000200 m 2 V −1 s −1 , or 2.00 cm 2 V −1 s −1 . Using 52.0 ms directly instead gives 1.923 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , approximately 3.85% lower. The arithmetic demonstrates why the time definition matters. It does not establish a universal correction of 2 ms: real corrections depend on instrument geometry and settings. If N equals the explicitly chosen N 0 , K 0 equals K in this example; otherwise apply the density factor. What collision cross section means A mobility-derived collision cross section (CCS, often Ω) is an effective ion–gas collision quantity derived through a physical model, commonly reported in Å 2 . It is sensitive to ion structure and ion–gas interactions, rather than simply the geometric silhouette of a neutral molecule. Under matching low-field conditions, the conversion depends on mobility, charge, temperature, gas density, and the ion–gas reduced mass. [1] Specify which ion was measured: [M+H] + , [M+Na] + , and [M−H] − are different species. Their CCS values are not interchangeable entries for “M.” A primary small-molecule drift-tube study measured multiple ion forms in nitrogen and used CCS as an additional candidate constraint. [6] If one ion has multiple mobility peaks, retain that distribution instead of silently replacing it with one unexplained average. Compare like with like Before interpreting a CCS difference, check ion composition and charge, bath gas, temperature, field regime, measurement method, and calibration provenance. For calibrated results, record calibrant identities, reference values, fitting procedure, and the range validated. Do not assume a calibration performs equally well far outside that range. Cross-laboratory drift-tube work demonstrates the value of standardized measurements; its measured performance does not become an accuracy guarantee for unrelated workflows. [2] Constructed comparison: a query gives 202 Å 2 and a candidate reference gives 200 Å 2 , a +1.0% difference relative to the reference. Whether that is acceptable depends on measurement uncertainty, reference uncertainty, bias, and a validated matching rule. Neither “within 2%” nor “within 1%” is a universal identification criterion. A helium reference and a nitrogen query should not be treated as directly interchangeable merely because both use Å 2 . Separation is not complete identification Some isomers separate; others overlap at the available resolving power. A single mobility peak does not prove sample purity. Multiple peaks can reflect distinct compounds, conformers, or different protonation-site populations, requiring additional evidence to distinguish those explanations. Source and transfer conditions can also change the ions entering the mobility region. Gas-phase structure therefore needs its own interpretation before being used to infer solution structure. [1] Use mobility alongside accurate mass, isotopes, retention, and diagnostic fragmentation. Agreement can narrow a candidate set; disagreement should trigger a check of ion identity and measurement comparability before a chemical conclusion. Check your understanding Two ions have equal CCS values. Must they be the same structure? No. Different structures can have overlapping CCS values, especially within finite uncertainty.
